domain: Applying signal-detection theory (a framework built for radar and sonar operators) to how forensic fingerprint examiners decide whether two prints 'match' — and what gets lost when a courtroom judgment is treated as a detection problem
topic: Applying signal-detection theory (a framework built for radar and sonar operators) to how forensic fingerprint examiners decide whether two prints 'match' — and what gets lost when a courtroom judgment is treated as a detection problem

source.title: Tips and tools for navigating hearing loss

movement.gist: Introduce signal-detection theory (SDT) from psychophysics/radar science — the 'signal amid noise, operator sets a threshold, hit rate vs false-alarm rate' apparatus — and describe how forensic scientists, stung by DNA-exoneration scandals, began importing it wholesale to model fingerprint examiners as detectors with adjustable criteria, promising to convert subjective 'expert judgment' into measurable performance curves.

Show the lens working: SDT-style studies reveal examiners have a genuine, quantifiable sensitivity to print similarity independent of their response bias, exposing that many 'errors' were criterion-setting problems (over-caution or overconfidence) rather than perceptual failure — a real, useful discrimination.

Expose the distortion: SDT assumes a stable, well-defined signal distribution generated independently of the observer, but a fingerprint 'signal' is partly constituted by the examiner's prior exposure to case context, the prosecutor's framing, and the print's own construction as evidence — the 'noise' floor keeps moving, which the model cannot represent.

Tally the cost: quantification bought real gains (identifying bias, enabling calibration training) but also let institutions certify examiners as 'validated detectors,' foreclosing scrutiny of the contextual contamination the model can't see — the thesis crystallizes here as refusal to accept that the numbers settle the courtroom question.

primary.axis: whether a match decision is a detection event (signal vs noise, quantifiable hit/miss rates) or an interpretive act (a narrative judgment embedded in institutional and adversarial context)
poles: fingerprint matching as situated interpretive judgment

secondary.axis: whether the appeal of quantifying examiner error (ROC curves, hit rates, false-alarm rates) is a genuine epistemic gain or a rhetorical laundering of uncertainty into the language of science

tension_system.interaction: the secondary tension supplies the mechanism by which the primary tension's resolution is forced: the very quantification that makes the lens seem to work is what reveals its distortion, so accepting the numbers means accepting the bill they carry.

family_realization.note: Perfect arc: lens imported (P1), yields real gains (P2), distortion exposed (P3), price named quietly (P4). Author tracking own use vs. examination of it throughout.

ending_behavior.note: Burden shifts: institutions now must answer why certification masks contextual contamination. 'I no longer accept' (P4) is aperture 'holds'—resolution costed, not resolved.

voice_consistency.note: Elegiac insider authority throughout: 'those of us who trained examiners,' 'we imported it,' 'we should not pretend.' Refusal of generic academy-speak maintained.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1(B)=premature_closure; Q2(C)=half_truth; Q3(B)=wrong_cost_type; Q4(A)=moderate_extremism; Q5(D)=stance_misread. All traps require passage-locating work.

explanation_quality.note: Every elimination cites specific passage coordinates (P1-4) and names mechanism: 'twists separation into irrelevance,' 'conflates institutions' use with author's acceptance.' No vague rejections.

answers.reasoning: Passage argues theory gave real but partial gains, hiding unscored contamination via certification.

Directly follows text: certification became wall hiding contamination the model can't score.
Critique rests on premise that fixed distributions can't represent observer-created signals.
